children: Radiant Logistics reported fourth fiscal quarter revenue of $261.4 million and GAAP net income attributable to the company of $7.5 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $10.4 million and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.15; the company entered fiscal 2027 with no net debt following an amended $200 million revolving credit facility. Management highlighted broad-based quarter-over-quarter momentum across U.S. forwarding, international airfreight strength and new agent initiatives.
Revenue: $261.4 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, up 18.5% from $220.6 million a year earlier.
GAAP gross profit: $64.4 million for the quarter; GAAP gross profit margin: 24.6%.
Adjusted gross profit: $66.8 million for the quarter (adjusted gross profit percentage: 25.6%).
Net income attributable to Radiant Logistics: $7.5 million, or $0.16 basic and $0.15 diluted per share for the quarter.
Adjusted EBITDA: $10.4 million for the quarter; adjusted EBITDA margin (as % of adjusted gross profit): 15.5%.
U.S. forwarding operations drove quarter-over-quarter improvement, with notable contribution from domestic and international service offerings and international airfreight strength.

Capacity tightening in North American truckload and intermodal markets contributed to rising spot rates and tender rejections, trends management views as supportive for domestic brokerage operations if sustained.

Launched a new independent agent program at Radiant Road & Rail to expand the company’s agent model into truck brokerage and intermodal, aiming to recruit logistics entrepreneurs with access to Radiant’s carrier network and platforms.
Expanded adoption of Navegate platform among enterprise customers (one enterprise customer managing over 1,400 vendors) as a catalyst for visibility and supply-chain management improvements.

International developments — including disruptions to ocean routes and evolving tariff complexity — increased demand for customs brokerage and compliance services; the quarter also saw elevated airfreight demand tied to disaster relief activity in the Western Pacific.
